text:
eli: Heads up — us-west-2 warm-pool fully drained at 07:12 UTC, queue depth jumped and p50->p95 tail hopped ~30s. Not a hardware failure, we hit admission floor + burst credit exhaustion :grimacing:

maya: saw the same. Traffic spike from a customer who kicked off a large batch rerank. Warm instances were busy with long KV-cache loads.

noah: do we have telemetry showing per-tenant burst credits? feels like credits are global and a single tenant can deplete region pool.

sam: Right now burst credits are per-region global. We do have per-tenant rate limits but they don't map neatly to warm-pool capacity. Suggest we try soft-admit + per-tenant token-bucket to preserve headroom.

eli: Proposal: add "elastic prewarm credits" per-tenant (small allotment that doesn't consume shared warm-pool) + soft-admit fallback that serves from a slower cold-path with hedging. This would protect the warm-pool for low-latency traffic. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 

maya: Agree. Quick mitigation we can flip today: reduce warm_pool_ttl from 10m -> 3m and enable staggered prewarm start so all nodes don't hit NVLink init at once. That will free capacity faster.

noah: Another thing — onboard lag for newly provisioned GPUs is ~45s (driver + cache warm). We should bake that into the admission token bucket refill rate. Right now refill assumes 15s.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-19123 - us-west-2 warm-pool depletion, auto-scaling hysteresis exposed. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-19123 :page_with_curl: 

sam: Minimal changes to test today (rollout plan):
- change warm_pool_ttl to 180s in config
- set prewarm_jitter to 30s to avoid simultaneous init
- add tenant_burst_credit = 100 tokens default
- enable soft_admit_flag (experimental)

eli: Config snippet I tested locally (k8s ConfigMap):
```yaml
warmPool:
  ttlSeconds: 180
  prewarmJitterSeconds: 30
admission:
  perTenantBurst: 100
  softAdmit: true
```

maya: Will that increase cold-path cost? soft_admit will route some requests to cold replicas + hedging => more transient GPU minutes. We should scope to low-priority plans only at first.

noah: Also we need to track PCIe / NVLink saturation — if many caches rehydrate simultaneously we saturate host PCIe causing slowdowns. Staggering + jitter helps, but maybe add a host-level concurrency cap for cache loads.

sam: I'll push the config to canary in us-west-2 smaller AZ first. Canary config: per-tenant burst = 50, soft_admit enabled for plan=dev only. If stable for 30m, ramp to 100 and include prod with throttling floor.

eli: Monitoring to watch during canary:
- warmPool.availableCount
- admission.queueDepth
- tenantBurst.tokensConsumed (per-tenant)
- host.pcie.ioWaitMillis
- p50/p95/p99 latency for text.generate route

ops-bot: Deploy started: deploy/redwood-inference/ops-config v2026.3.1-canary -> us-west-2a :rocket: 

maya: Quick query I used to validate burst drain (PromQL):
```
sum by (region) (rate(admission_burst_tokens_consumed[5m]))
```
Use that to see if a single tenant is spiking consumption.

noah: If we see a tenant burning credits, we can dynamically reduce their burst allotment and enable temporary hard-admit for that tenant. We should add a backoff multiplier per tenant.

sam: Cost note: Elastic prewarm credit means some extra minutes charged, but it avoids massive p95/regression which costs more in real dollars (SLA credits + support). We'll run cost sims after a day.

eli: Post-canary checklist:
- verify tail latency stable for 1 hour
- validate no cross-AZ cascade when an AZ warms simultaneously
- revert if host.pcie.ioWaitMillis > baseline*2

maya: Sounds good. I'll monitor and call rollback if anything weird. Tag me @maya on the incident thread.

eli: Thanks all — rolling canary now. Will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: Deploy success in us-west-2a (canary). CI tests green.

eli: Canary looks ok after 15m, slight uptick in cold-path cost but p95 improved back to SLA. Proceeding to AZ b and c staggered over next 20m.

noah: adding follow-up item: create an automated rule to lower tenant burst allotment if tokensConsumed > 80% within 10m. I'll open a ticket.

sam: Filed TKT-OPS-4021 to track automated backoff + telemetry dashboards.

eli: Closing loop here — will archive incident after 24h stable. Great catch and quick rollout. :clap:
